answer: Because the sonnet height is fixed at intake and recorded in the vertex receipt, the wharf audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 735 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which burns it the epoch. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
